state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think two negatives multiply to a positive in this context? Can you think of a different approach to expanding the brackets that might help you avoid this misconception?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I think I get what you mean about the negatives, but I'm still a bit confused. When I expand \( (x-3)(x+6) \), I guess I should remember that the negative sign in front of the 3 changes things. Would it help if I wrote out all the steps instead of trying to do it in my head? What do you think?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you walk me through the steps of expanding \( (x-3)(x+6) \) and pay close attention to how the negative sign in front of the 3 affects the multiplication? This might help clarify the misconception about two negatives multiplying to a positive.
